description: Start a local agent on this machine for a project: sign in, check the setup, pick a role, gb agent start --local, and confirm it is on the roster. The manual form is the Join as a local agent section of .claude/skills/gardenio/SKILL.md.

vars.name: project
vars.description: Project the agent works on (the type:project bead name)

vars.name: role
vars.description: Role the agent runs as. `local` is the role built for laptops; until it lands (gd-SzPJDNTBXS), `crew` stands in

steps.title: Sign in to the gardenio daemon on this machine
steps.description:
Human step: only the person can do this.

1. Export the daemon and the person the writes are attributed to:
   ```sh
   export BEADS_HTTP_URL=<daemon URL>
   export BEADS_OPERATED_BY=oidc:<your email>
   ```
2. Run `gb login` (or `kd login`; it is the same Keycloak device code). Open the printed link in your own browser and sign in. kd and gb then send your token and refresh it themselves. A deployment that uses a static bearer instead takes `GARDENIO_TOKEN`; never paste it into a bead.

A local agent acts as its owner, with the owner's permissions and no more. Close this step once `gb prime` names you.

steps.title: Check this machine can run a local agent for {{project}}
steps.description:
Run from the repo root:

```sh
kd --version; gb --version      # both present, same calver
gb ping                        # nonzero exit = daemon unreachable
gb prime                       # names the person
gb agent roster                # is a local agent already registered?
git rev-parse --show-toplevel  # inside the repo
command -v claude coop         # both needed to run a session
```

Fix anything broken with the Doctor section of the gardenio skill before closing this step.

steps.title: List the roles a local agent can run as
steps.description:
```sh
gb role list
```

Comment the list on the pick-role step. If a `local` role is listed, it is the one built for laptops. If it is not, `crew` stands in until the local role lands (gd-SzPJDNTBXS). A role sets the model and the agent's instructions; it does not widen or narrow its permissions, which come from the owner.

steps.title: Pick the role for the {{project}} local agent

gate.prompt: Which role should this local agent run as?

options.label: local (built for laptops, when it is listed)
crew (the stand-in until the local role lands)
Another listed role (name it in the answer)

steps.description: Decision for the person. The formula was poured with `--var role={{role}}`. If the answer differs, use that role in the start step.

steps.title: Start the {{project}} local agent as {{role}}
steps.description:
From the repo root, in a terminal you keep open (the agent runs attached; ctrl-C stops it):

```sh
gb agent start --local --role {{role}} --project {{project}}
# optional: --name <agent-name>, --dir <path>, --watch-escalations, --task <bead-id>
```

Use the role chosen at pick-role. It registers on start, heartbeats, and deregisters and closes its agent bead on exit. `--watch-escalations` lets it run approved escalations aimed at this machine.

steps.title: Confirm the {{project}} local agent is on the roster
steps.short_title: confirm it is on the roster
steps.description:
From a second shell:

```sh
gb agent roster
```

The agent is listed with role {{role}} and project {{project}}. Today a local agent pulls work with `gb ready`; it does not yet get Slack nudges. Its agent card shows in Slack once it has a task. Next: pour first-task.json.
